Passwordless sudo rule dropped into /etc/sudoers.d (Miasma privilege escalation) AIExploitation High
Detects creation of files under /etc/sudoers.d containing 'NOPASSWD:ALL' (specifically the 'runner ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' string the Miasma payload writes), and the bind-mount-to-/mnt technique used to deposit the sudoers fragment. Sigma covers the process-create path; KQL covers both file-write and sudoers-validation chains. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact verbatim code block: "echo 'runner ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' > ... && chmod 0440 /mnt/runner" and "sudo -n true". The 'NOPASSWD:ALL' string combined with a /etc/sudoers.d or /mnt/ write target is the article-specific signature; this rule should not fire on legitimate config-mgmt because we filter on node/bun/shell parents.
ATT&CKT1548.003 T1098
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ansible/Chef/Puppet runs deploying CI runner sudoers fragments at provisioning time
  • Cloud-init bake scripts on AMI build that legitimately add 'runner ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL'
  • Packer / image-builder workflows constructing sudoers files during golden-image creation
  • Kubernetes self-hosted runner Helm charts that templatize sudoers.d entries
  • Manual sysadmin troubleshooting via 'visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/runner'
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ansible","chef-client","puppet-agent","cloud-init","packer","kubelet")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("ansible","chef-client","puppet-agent","cloud-init","packer")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: confirm parent process is node/bun/sh and not ansible-playbook, chef-client, puppet, cloud-init, packer, or kubelet (legitimate deployers); the article-specific signal is the bind-mount via /mnt. 2. CONTAIN: remove the rogue sudoers fragment, terminate the offending process tree, freeze the runner instance and preserve disk for forensics, revoke any tokens cached in /home/runner/.config and /home/runner/work/_temp. 3. HUNT: pivot to subsequent 'sudo -n true' and 'sudo sh -c' invocations from the same AccountName, and to /etc/hosts writes for security-vendor blackholes (the follow-on Miasma defense-evasion step).
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "NOPASSWD:ALL"
       and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/etc/sudoers.d","/mnt/","sudoers")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FolderPath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
       or (FolderPath startswith "/mnt/" and FileName has_any ("runner","sudoers"))
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","tee","cp","mv","dd")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName_proc = InitiatingProcessFileName)
| project Timestamp, Source, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
union
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "NOPASSWD:ALL"
       and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/etc/sudoers.d","/mnt/","sudoers")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
       or (TargetFilePath startswith "/mnt/" and TargetFileName has_any ("runner","sudoers"))
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","tee")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ActingProcessCommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine)
| project TimeGenerated, Source, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Passwordless Sudo Rule Drop via /etc/sudoers.d (Miasma)
id: c4f2a51d-86b3-4c19-9e7a-2d8b6f3c4a91
description: Detects the Miasma payload writing 'NOPASSWD:ALL' rules into /etc/sudoers.d (often via a bind-mount of /mnt), granting passwordless root to the runner/maintainer account.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1548.003
  - attack.t1098
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains: 'NOPASSWD:ALL'
  selection_target:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/etc/sudoers.d'
      - '/mnt/'
      - 'sudoers'
  filter_pkg_install:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/apt'
      - '/dpkg'
      - '/yum'
      - '/dnf'
      - '/rpm'
  condition: selection_cmd and selection_target and not filter_pkg_install
falsepositives:
  - Configuration management (Ansible, Chef, Puppet) deploying sudoers fragments
  - Cloud-init / packer image bake steps writing CI runner sudo rules
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:*NOPASSWD\:ALL* (@process.command_line:*\/etc\/sudoers.d* OR @process.command_line:*\/mnt\/* OR @process.command_line:*sudoers*) -@process.executable.path:(/usr/bin/apt OR /usr/bin/dpkg OR /usr/bin/yum OR /usr/bin/dnf) -@process.command_line:*ansible*
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten)
| (regex("NOPASSWD:ALL", field=CommandLine) AND regex("(/etc/sudoers\\.d|/mnt/|sudoers)", field=CommandLine))
   OR (TargetFileName=/\/etc\/sudoers\.d\// OR TargetFileName=/\/mnt\/(runner|sudoers)/)
| ContextImageFileName=/\/(node|bun|sh|bash|tee|cp|dd)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*NOPASSWD:ALL*" AND (Processes.process="*/etc/sudoers.d*" OR Processes.process="*/mnt/*" OR Processes.process="*runner ALL=(ALL)*")) OR (Processes.process_name="mount" AND Processes.process="*bind*" AND Processes.process="*/etc/sudoers.d*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*NOPASSWD:ALL*" AND (Processes.process="*/etc/sudoers.d*" OR Processes.process="*/mnt/*" OR Processes.process="*runner ALL=(ALL)*")) OR (Processes.process_name="mount" AND Processes.process="*bind*" AND Processes.process="*/etc/sudoers.d*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Security vendor domain blackhole written to /etc/hosts from non-admin process AIExploitation High
Detects the Miasma payload's defense-evasion step where it pipes 'echo 127.0.0.1 <vendor>' through sudo to append to /etc/hosts, blackholing telemetry/update domains for installed security products. Anchored on /etc/hosts writes initiated by node/bun/shell processes. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim code block: 'sudo sh -c "echo \'127.0.0.1 <vendor>\' >> /etc/hosts"' under the Neutralize Security product monitoring comment. The combination of /etc/hosts + 127.0.0.1 + append from a node/bun/sh parent on a CI runner is highly article-specific.
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1565.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dockerfile RUN steps editing /etc/hosts inside container build layers
  • Cloud-init / userdata adding loopback overrides for local services on VM bootstrap
  • Vagrant / minikube provisioners writing 127.0.0.1 entries for dev hostnames
  • Local dev sysadmins overriding production domains to point at staging
  • Kubernetes coredns config-test scripts editing /etc/hosts in a debug pod
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("docker build","buildkit","vagrant","minikube")
| where DeviceName !startswith "builder-" and DeviceName !startswith "packer-"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: capture the appended /etc/hosts line(s); cross-reference the blackholed domain against your EDR/AV vendor's update/telemetry domain list (CrowdStrike, Defender, SentinelOne, Trend) — if the domain is a security product, treat as confirmed compromise. 2. CONTAIN: restore /etc/hosts from a known-good baseline, isolate the host, kill the node/bun parent tree, snapshot disk for forensics, and rotate any creds reachable from the host. 3. HUNT: pivot on InitiatingProcessFolderPath for the dropper script that issued the command, then DeviceProcessEvents for follow-on 'sudo -n true' validation and IMDS / GitHub API calls in the next 5 minutes.
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "/etc/hosts"
       and ProcessCommandLine has "127.0.0.1"
       and ProcessCommandLine has_any (">>"," tee ","echo ")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","zsh","sudo")
       or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","bun","npm")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FolderPath == "/etc/" and FileName == "hosts"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","tee","sudo")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, Source, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
union
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "/etc/hosts"
       and ActingProcessCommandLine has "127.0.0.1"
       and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (">>"," tee ","echo ")
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","sudo")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetFilePath == "/etc/hosts"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","tee")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ActingProcessCommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine)
| project TimeGenerated, Source, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: /etc/hosts Blackhole Write from Node or Bun Process (Miasma Defense Evasion)
id: 7e3a1b94-c52f-4d68-b1ae-9f4d8c2e7b15
description: Detects the Miasma payload writing 127.0.0.1 entries to /etc/hosts (typically to blackhole security vendor update/telemetry domains) via a node/bun/shell pipeline using echo + sudo + redirect.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.t1565.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_target:
    CommandLine|contains: '/etc/hosts'
  selection_loopback:
    CommandLine|contains: '127.0.0.1'
  selection_write:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '>>'
      - ' tee '
      - 'echo '
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/node'
      - '/bun'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/sudo'
      - '/npm'
  condition: selection_target and selection_loopback and selection_write and selection_parent
falsepositives:

  - Internal IT scripts overriding DNS for staging environments
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:*\/etc\/hosts* @process.command_line:*127.0.0.1* (@process.command_line:*\>\>* OR @process.command_line:*tee* OR @process.command_line:*echo*) (@process.parent.name:(node OR bun OR sh OR bash OR sudo OR npm) OR @ParentImage:(*\node OR *\bun OR *\sh OR *\bash))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| regex("/etc/hosts", field=CommandLine)
| regex("127\\.0\\.0\\.1", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(>>|\\stee\\s|echo\\s)", field=CommandLine)
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|bun|sh|bash|dash|sudo|npm)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/etc/hosts*" AND Processes.process="*127.0.0.1*" AND (Processes.process="*>>*" OR Processes.process="*tee*" OR Processes.process_name="echo") AND (Processes.parent_process_name="node" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bun" OR Processes.parent_process_name="sh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bash") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/etc/hosts*" AND Processes.process="*127.0.0.1*" AND (Processes.process="*>>*" OR Processes.process="*tee*" OR Processes.process_name="echo") AND (Processes.parent_process_name="node" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bun" OR Processes.parent_process_name="sh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bash") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Public GitHub repo creation matching Miasma 'adjective-creature-N' exfil pattern AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the Miasma exfiltration channel: creation of a public GitHub repository under a victim's account named with the adjective-creature-N convention and/or containing the 'Miasma: The Spreading Blight' description, followed by commits to results/<timestamp>-<counter>.json paths. Pivots on CloudAppEvents / GitHub audit logs. Rationale: Anchored on Phase 10 of the article: 'Creates a public repo in the victim’s GitHub account ("Miasma: The Spreading Blight") and commits stolen credential JSON to results/<timestamp>-<counter>.json' and the adjective-creature-<0-99999> naming convention called out in the kill-chain reconstruction. Both the regex name pattern and the 'Miasma' string have no legitimate use in this org's GitHub footprint.
ATT&CKT1567.001 T1102.002
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer creating a public repo for a personal toy project that happens to match adjective-creature-N (e.g. 'happy-otter-42') — visibility=public filter helps but is not exhaustive
  • GitHub default repo suggestion using fun random names (rare, normally takes 'fluffy-octopus' shape with 2 tokens, not 3 with a number)
  • Hackathon teams using a generated team-name + entry-number convention
  • Bot-driven repo creation by legitimate automation (filter on AccountDisplayName not being github-actions[bot])
  • Internal blue-team exercises planting decoy repos matching this pattern
Suppression filter
| where AccountDisplayName !has "[bot]"
| where Description !has_any ("hackathon","team-","toy-","playground")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: open the matched repo URL and inspect results/*.json contents — if present, treat as confirmed exfiltration; capture the file SHAs and the maintainer's PAT inventory. 2. CONTAIN: revoke ALL PATs and OIDC-trusted tokens for the maintainer account, force a GitHub session reset, delete the public repo (after preserving evidence), and disable the maintainer's npm publish rights until investigation completes. 3. HUNT: pivot on the maintainer account for additional repo creates, new .github/setup.js commits across owned repos, and any npm publishes within the same 24h — the worm tries to spread to all maintainer-owned packages.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType has_any ("Create repository","RepositoryCreate","repo.create")
| extend RepoName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).repo)
| extend Visibility = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).visibility)
| extend Description = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).description)
| where Visibility =~ "public"
| where RepoName matches regex @"^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-\d{1,5}$"
   or Description has_any ("Miasma","Spreading Blight","The Spreading Blight")
   or RawEventData has "results/" and RawEventData has ".json"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, RepoName, Visibility, Description, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
// Pre-req: GitHub Enterprise audit log connector ingesting into a custom GitHubAudit_CL table, or using OfficeActivity for GitHub via Cloud App Security
let GitHubLogs = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where OfficeWorkload has_any ("GitHub","github")
           or RecordType has "GitHub";
GitHubLogs
| where Operation has_any ("repo.create","RepositoryCreate","Create repository")
| extend RepoName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).repo)
| extend Visibility = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).visibility)
| extend Description = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).description)
| where Visibility =~ "public"
| where RepoName matches regex @"^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-\d{1,5}$"
   or Description has_any ("Miasma","Spreading Blight")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, RepoName, Visibility, Description, Operation
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:github @action:(repo.create OR RepositoryCreate) @repo.visibility:public (@repo.name:/^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-\d{1,5}$/ OR @repo.description:(*Miasma* OR *"Spreading Blight"*))
CLOUD
`github_audit_log` action="repo.create" visibility="public" (repo="*-*-*" OR description="*Miasma*" OR description="*Spreading Blight*") | rex field=repo "^(?<adj>[a-z]+)-(?<creature>[a-z]+)-(?<idx>\d{1,5})$" | where isnotnull(idx) AND idx>=0 AND idx<=99999 | stats min(_time) as firstSeen, count by user, repo, description, visibility | sort - firstSeen
Worm-injected .github/setup.js commit with 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]' message AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the Miasma worm's lateral-movement technique: commits adding a .github/setup.js file via the GitHub Git Data API, authored as 'github-actions@github.com' with the verbatim message 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]'. These commits appear across non-protected branches in victim-owned repos and skip CI by design. Rationale: Anchored on Phase 11 of the kill-chain reconstruction: 'Hunt for commits adding .github/setup.js authored as github-actions@github.com with message chore: update dependencies [skip ci]'. The exact file path, author email, and commit message are verbatim worm signatures with no legitimate corollary — Dependabot uses a different author identity and never adds setup.js.
ATT&CKT1080 T1195.002 T1098.004
Data sourcesChange
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine github-actions bot updating workflow files (would NOT touch .github/setup.js)
  • Internal CI automation re-using the github-actions identity for housekeeping commits with similar message wording
  • Dependabot rebase commits (these author as dependabot[bot], not github-actions)
  • Repo templates that ship with .github/setup.js as a legitimate bootstrap script
  • Developers manually committing as the github-actions identity for testing (rare — requires PAT misuse)
Suppression filter
| where ObjectName !endswith "-template" and ObjectName !contains "boilerplate"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: inspect the .github/setup.js diff — if it contains obfuscated JS, eval(), Buffer.from(base64), or fetch to api.github.com / bun.sh, treat as confirmed worm injection. 2. CONTAIN: revoke the OIDC token / PAT that authored the commit, revert the commit across ALL affected repos (use the GitHub API to delete or revert the matching SHA), force-rotate the maintainer's GitHub session, audit npm publishes signed by exchanged OIDC tokens from this maintainer in the last 7 days. 3. HUNT: enumerate ALL repos owned by the maintainer for additional .github/setup.js files or matching commit messages, and check Sigstore/Rekor transparency log for unexpected SLSA provenance entries against the maintainer's npm packages.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType has_any ("git.push","push","PushCommit","Push")
| extend Files = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).added)
| extend Message = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).message)
| extend AuthorEmail = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).author_email)
| where Files has ".github/setup.js"
   or (Message =~ "chore: update dependencies [skip ci]" and AuthorEmail =~ "github-actions@github.com")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, ObjectName, Files, Message, AuthorEmail, IPAddress, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
let GitHubLogs = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where OfficeWorkload has "GitHub" or RecordType has "GitHub";
GitHubLogs
| where Operation has_any ("git.push","push","PushCommit")
| extend Files = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).added)
| extend Message = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).message)
| extend AuthorEmail = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).author_email)
| where Files has ".github/setup.js"
   or (Message =~ "chore: update dependencies [skip ci]" and AuthorEmail =~ "github-actions@github.com")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ObjectId, Files, Message, AuthorEmail, ClientIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc

source:github @action:(git.push OR push OR PushCommit) (@commit.added:*.github\/setup.js* OR (@commit.author.email:github-actions@github.com AND @commit.message:"chore: update dependencies [skip ci]"))
CLOUD
`github_audit_log` (action="git.push" OR action="push") (commit_message="chore: update dependencies [skip ci]" OR added_files="*.github/setup.js*") | rex max_match=1 field=added_files "(?<setupjs>\.github/setup\.js)" | where isnotnull(setupjs) OR (commit_author_email="github-actions@github.com" AND commit_message="chore: update dependencies [skip ci]") | stats min(_time) as firstSeen, dc(repo) as repoCount, values(repo) as repos by user, commit_author_email | sort - firstSeen
Destructive 'rm -rf ~' or Miasma honeytoken tripwire from node/bun process tree AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the Miasma destructive fail-safe: 'rm -rf ~/' / 'rm -rf ~/Documents' invoked by a node or bun process tree (often after the planted honeytoken 'IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner' is touched). Also directly matches the honeytoken string in any process command line or file content. Rationale: Anchored on Phase 12 of the kill-chain reconstruction: the verbatim honeytoken string 'IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner' and the destructive commands 'rm -rf ~/' and 'rm -rf ~/Documents'. The honeytoken string is unique to this campaign with zero legitimate use; the rm-rf combined with a node/bun parent is the article's specific destructive-tripwire shape, distinguishing it from generic CI workspace cleanup.
ATT&CKT1485 T1491.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer cleanup scripts running 'rm -rf ~/.cache' or 'rm -rf ~/tmp' (different sub-paths, often interactive)
  • CI workspace teardown scripts that clean ~/work or ~/agent directories (different target shape, parent usually pipeline runner)
  • Containerized build images doing 'rm -rf $HOME/.npm' to shrink layers (parent is docker/buildkit, not node)
  • Local nuke-and-pave dev scripts run manually by an engineer in a terminal (parent is shell, not node/bun)
  • Red-team engagement tooling intentionally testing destructive behaviors
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("docker build","buildkit") and ProcessCommandLine has "$HOME/.npm")
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName == "systemd" and AccountName == "runner" and ProcessCommandLine has "~/work")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: confirm honeytoken string match (zero-FP signal) or pivot on the rm -rf process tree to verify node/bun grandparent; check DeviceFileEvents for the burst of deletions in ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config/gcloud in the seconds before/after. 2. CONTAIN: kill the entire process tree immediately (ProcessId + all descendants), snapshot the disk while still recoverable (filesystem journal may have file refs), isolate from network, alert the user/maintainer that their account is compromised. 3. HUNT: pivot on the maintainer's GitHub PAT and npm OIDC tokens for any republish events in the last 24h, check Sigstore/Rekor for unexpected signing entries, and enumerate all victim-owned repos for the .github/setup.js worm payload.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("rm","rm.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "-rf"
          and (ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s~/?(\s|$)"
               or ProcessCommandLine has " $HOME"
               or ProcessCommandLine has "~/Documents"
               or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s/home/[^/\s]+/?(\s|$)"))
      or ProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","zsh","npm")
     or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","bun","npm","yarn","pnpm")
     or ProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, 
    InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
    InitiatingProcessParentCreationTime
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessName endswith "rm" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "-rf"
          and (ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s~/?(\s|$)"
               or ActingProcessCommandLine has " $HOME"
               or ActingProcessCommandLine has "~/Documents"))
      or ActingProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","npm")
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma Destructive Tripwire - rm -rf Home from Node or Bun
id: 6c8e3a17-9b42-4d51-a73c-1f9d5b8e7c4a
description: Detects 'rm -rf ~/' or honeytoken-triggered destructive deletions executed from a node/bun/npm process tree, signaling the Miasma fail-safe that wipes the maintainer's home directory when the planted honeytoken 'IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner' is touched or revoked.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1485
  - attack.t1491.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_honeytoken:
    CommandLine|contains: 'IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner'
  selection_rm:
    Image|endswith: '/rm'
    CommandLine|contains: '-rf'
  selection_target_home:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' ~/'
      - ' $HOME'
      - '~/Documents'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/node'
      - '/bun'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/npm'
  condition: selection_honeytoken or (selection_rm and selection_target_home and selection_parent)
falsepositives:
  - Developer cleanup scripts (very rare with node parent)
  - CI workspace cleanup running 'rm -rf $HOME/work/*' (different target shape)
level: critical
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE ((@process.name:rm @process.command_line:*\-rf* (@process.command_line:*\ \~\/* OR @process.command_line:*\ \$HOME* OR @process.command_line:*\~\/Documents*) (@process.parent.name:(node OR bun OR sh OR bash OR npm))) OR @process.command_line:*IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (regex("IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner", field=CommandLine))
   OR (ImageFileName=/\/rm$/i AND regex("\\-rf", field=CommandLine) AND regex("(\\s~\\/?|\\s\\$HOME|~\\/Documents)", field=CommandLine) AND ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|bun|sh|bash|npm)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName, ParentCommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name="rm" AND Processes.process="*-rf*" AND (Processes.process="* ~/*" OR Processes.process="* $HOME*" OR Processes.process="*~/Documents*")) OR Processes.process="*IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner*") AND (Processes.parent_process_name="node" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bun" OR Processes.parent_process_name="sh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bash" OR Processes.parent_process_name="npm") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name="rm" AND Processes.process="*-rf*" AND (Processes.process="* ~/*" OR Processes.process="* $HOME*" OR Processes.process="*~/Documents*")) OR Processes.process="*IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner*") AND (Processes.parent_process_name="node" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bun" OR Processes.parent_process_name="sh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bash" OR Processes.parent_process_name="npm") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7") or SHA1 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7") or MD5 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7") or SHA1 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7") or MD5 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45247")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45247")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
